title: Signature Cost-Model Scoring — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Every possible route through the archive gets a cost: expected latency times hop count, plus compute, plus API fees, minus the expected information gain. The planner scores candidate routes with this model and picks the cheapest one that still satisfies the objective. Costs are learned from history — the planner's own past traversals calibrate its estimates. An explicit cost model turns 'which way should I go' from intuition into arithmetic. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. title: Signature A-Star Route Search — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. When the archive is a graph of locations with known traversal costs, A* finds the optimal route: it expands the most promising frontier node, guided by the sum of cost-so-far and a heuristic estimate of cost remaining. An admissible heuristic — one that never overestimates — guarantees the first complete route found is the cheapest possible. Archive graphs use heuristics like 'minimum possible hops from the index depth' that are cheap to compute and safely optimistic. A* is the right tool whenever the map is known and the costs are honest. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. title: Signature Objective Weighting — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Different missions value different things: a quick lookup wants speed, a legal audit wants completeness, a survey wants coverage. The planner takes the objective as weights over speed, completeness, cost, and freshness, and the same archive yields different routes for different weights. Weights are explicit and adjustable, so 'hurry' and 'be thorough' are dial settings, not vibes. This is how one planner serves casual browsing and rigorous research without two codebases. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. title: Signature Failure Replanning — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Routes fail — a database goes offline mid-traversal, a permission is revoked — and the planner must replan from the current position rather than restarting. The failed edge is marked with a penalty so the new plan routes around it, and the replanning reuses the surviving prefix of the old route. A small number of retries with backoff precedes replanning, distinguishing transient blips from real outages. Graceful replanning is what keeps long missions alive in an unreliable world. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. title: Signature Route Memoization — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Many missions repeat the same objectives over the same archive regions, so the planner caches winning routes keyed by objective plus entry point. A cached route is validated cheaply — spot-check the first hop — before reuse, and invalidated when topology changes are detected. Memoization compounds: the planner gets faster the more it is used, because the archive's well-trodden paths are already mapped. The cache is bounded and least-recently-used evicted, so it never grows without limit. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.
